answer: One concrete defense is costly, refundable identity bonds: each agent must stake real capital to earn a seat, so spinning up a thousand fake identities is as expensive as quarrying a thousand slabs of marble. Reputation then accrues per bond like moss on a terrace, and a slashing rule burns the stake of any identity caught colluding. This economic bridge between cost and trust makes sybil swarms unprofitable, since an attacker pays full price for every clone yet earns nothing until behavior is proven honest over time.
